def factor_smoothed_cycle_deviation_volume(df):
    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np
    df_copy = df.copy()
    sma200 = df_copy["close"].rolling(window=200, min_periods=1).mean()
    high = df_copy["high"]
    low = df_copy["low"]
    close = df_copy["close"]
    tr1 = high - low
    tr2 = (high - close.shift(1)).abs()
    tr3 = (low - close.shift(1)).abs()
    true_range = pd.concat([tr1, tr2, tr3], axis=1).max(axis=1)
    atr200 = true_range.rolling(window=200, min_periods=1).mean()
    cycle_dev = (close - sma200) / atr200.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    smoothed_cycle_dev = cycle_dev.ewm(span=3, adjust=False).mean()
    _, _, vol_ratio = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(df_copy["volume"], window=20)
    factor = smoothed_cycle_dev * vol_ratio
    df_copy["factor_smoothed_cycle_deviation_volume"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_smoothed_cycle_deviation_volume"]
description: The parent's core mechanism uses a long-term cycle deviation (close minus 200-day SMA, normalized by 200-day ATR) and scales it by a continuous volume ratio to confirm moves. This mutation smooths the raw cycle deviation with a short exponential moving average (span=3) before volume scaling. The EMA reduces noise in the deviation series, improving the signal stability and potentially enhancing IC and MI while preserving the rank stability (RankICIR) and the volume-confirmation logic of the parent.
